Triple Light Laser Cannon: 450 m range, 15 DMG Medium Laser Cannon: 650 m range, 12 DMG

Discord Missile: 750 m range, no shield penetration, 5 DMG, 15 m AOE Applies -33% HP debuff to fighter/bomber/gunship for 30s.

The Droid Tri-Fighter, designed by Colicoid Creation Nest, is a highly advanced unmanned space superiority starfighter built to outclass earlier droid designs. Manufactured by Phlac-Arphocc Automata Industries and Colla Designs, Tri-Fighters were far more complex and expensive than other droid counterparts, limiting their production numbers. Equipped with a significantly more sophisticated droid brain than the Vulture Droid, they demonstrate faster reaction times and far greater combat efficiency. Extremely small and compact, the Tri-Fighter combines incredible speed and maneuverability with a heavy weapons loadout. Armed with a central medium laser cannon, three wing-mounted light laser cannons, and Discord Missiles, they excel as interceptors, performing high-speed hit-and-run strikes against vulnerable targets such as bombers and gunships.

Required Planets (CIS, Underworld, Rebel, Neutral, Empire): Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost

The Variable Geometry Self-Propelled Battle Droid Mk. I, better known as the Vulture Droid, is a small unmanned starfighter that relies on overwhelming numbers to defeat its enemies. Lightly armored and armed, it compensates with high speed, strong maneuverability, and a small target profile that makes it difficult to hit in a dogfight. Produced in untold millions by Baktoid Armor Workshop and Haor Chall Engineering, Vulture Droids were a mainstay of Trade Federation naval forces before becoming a core component of the Confederacy’s war machine. Best employed in large groups, Vulture squadrons can overwhelm isolated enemies, but struggle in one-on-one engagements against even poorly trained organic pilots.

Required Planets (CIS, Underworld, Rebel, Neutral, Empire, Republic): Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost

The Variable Geometry Self-Propelled Battle Droid Mk. II, better known as the Heavy Vulture Droid, is a small unmanned starfighter that relies on overwhelming numbers to defeat its enemies. Based on the original Mk. I design, this variant has been modified to carry Discord Missiles, greatly improving its effectiveness against enemy starfighters. Lightly armored and armed, it compensates with high speed, strong maneuverability, and a small target profile that makes it difficult to hit in dogfights. Produced in untold millions by Baktoid Armor Workshop and Haor Chall Engineering, Heavy Vulture Droids serve as an upgraded component of the Confederacy’s war machine. Best employed in large groups, Vulture squadrons can overwhelm isolated enemies, but struggle in one-on-one engagements against even poorly trained organic pilots.

Required Planets: Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost

The Alpha-3 Nimbus-class Interceptor, better known as the V-Wing, is a fast, agile starfighter with exceptional survivability for its class. Equipped with rapidly recharging shields and an onboard astromech, it can outlast most light interceptors in prolonged dogfights. Its light repeating laser cannons are highly effective against fragile targets, allowing it to quickly eliminate droid starfighters and other lightly armored craft. However, the lack of missiles or heavier weapons limits its effectiveness against shielded or durable opponents. While outdated by the Galactic Civil War, the V-Wing remains a capable interceptor, able to reliably contest modern light fighters when used in its intended role.

A high-performance starfighter designed by the Hapes Consortium, the Miy’Tok features an advanced power management system and dual solar sails that generate excess energy for its engines, shields, and weapons. This allows for extremely high speed, rapidly recharging shields, and repeating laser cannons capable of sustained, uninterrupted fire. These advantages come at a cost. The Miy’Tok’s handling is mediocre, and its large profile and light armor make it an easy target for enemies that manage to get behind it.

This unit is unaffected by nebulas.

The Aurek-class Tactical Strikefighter is an old, proven starfighter design whose lineage stretches back to the era of the Old Republic. Widely adopted and endlessly reproduced, the Aurek earned its reputation as a fast, nimble, and heavily armed craft, remaining in service long after more modern designs came and went. Cheap to manufacture, easy to maintain, and effective in combat, it is still commonly encountered in pirate fleets, planetary militias, and other irregular forces.

Armed with medium laser cannons on swiveling mounts and a proton torpedo launcher, the Aurek delivers a powerful opening strike capable of crippling enemy starfighters in a single pass. Its high speed and rapidly recharging shields allow it to disengage quickly after attacking, but its light hull leaves it vulnerable to fast interceptors and sustained missile fire that can overwhelm its defenses.

Anti-Starfighter Missile: 900 m range, no shield penetration, 25 DMG

Developed by Kuat Systems Engineering for the Republic, the R-22 “Spearhead” was designed to replace the V-19, Delta-7, and Eta-2 as part of a broader shift toward independent starfighter doctrine. Unlike its predecessors, the R-22 combined shielding, extreme maneuverability, and a compact profile with an integrated hyperdrive, eliminating the need for docking rings and allowing it to operate independently across multiple theaters. This made the Spearhead well suited to the Republic’s growing reliance on fast-deploying fleets and deep-space operations.

As the Clone Wars drew to a close, the program was abandoned, with the Imperial Navy rejecting it in favor of the cheaper TIE line built around mass production and carrier reliance. Diverted to civilian and black market sales, the R-22 found new life among rebel cells, criminal syndicates, and independent factions. With exceptional speed, agility, respectable shielding, and repeating laser cannons capable of extremely high rates of fire, it proved more than a match for contemporary starfighters, and its combat record would later influence Kuat’s next generation of interceptors, culminating in the RZ-1 A-Wing.

The Sith Aurora-class Starfighter is an ancient design believed to originate from early Sith Empire production, now constructed in limited numbers by hidden Sith-aligned factions. Small, lightweight, and built with little regard for pilot safety, the craft emphasizes speed and agility above all else. Lacking both shields and a hyperdrive, it relies entirely on maneuverability and its minimal target profile for survival.

Armed with only light laser cannons and protected by a fragile hull, the Sith Starfighter is individually weak but capable of reaching extreme speeds. It performs best when deployed in large numbers, overwhelming enemy defenses through sheer volume and rapid attack runs. Though crude by modern standards, its agility and low cost make it a persistent threat when massed together.

Developed by Incom as a simplified successor to the Clone Wars–era Z-95 CVI, the Z-95 Headhunter was designed to be inexpensive, rugged, and easy to mass-produce. Many of the complex and maintenance-heavy systems of its predecessor were deliberately stripped away, resulting in a straightforward general-purpose starfighter well suited to militias, planetary defense forces, and pirates. While clearly outclassed by modern starfighters, the Z-95 remains serviceable thanks to its reliability, wide availability, and flexible design. Of particular note is its modular ordnance launcher system, allowing the Headhunter to carry either missiles or torpedoes depending on mission requirements. Long past its prime, the Z-95 endures not through superiority, but through affordability, familiarity, and adaptability.

Developed from the standard Z-95 Headhunter, the Z-95 “Hullcracker” is a strike-focused variant that leverages the fighter’s modular ordnance launcher to replace concussion missiles with proton torpedoes. This simple modification allows the Hullcracker to function as a light, low-cost bomber capable of threatening capital ships and orbital installations. Poorly armored and lightly defended, it is undeniably crude by modern military standards, but its affordability and ease of maintenance have made it a favorite among pirates, criminal syndicates, and irregular forces. When deployed in numbers, the Hullcracker can overwhelm point defenses and deliver surprisingly devastating damage, ensuring it remains a threat that cannot be safely ignored.

The Variable Geometry Self-Propelled Battle Droid Mk. III, better known as the Hyena Droid Bomber, is a larger unmanned strike craft derived from the Vulture Droid design. Sharing the same general shape and performance characteristics, the Hyena trades some agility for increased payload capacity, with an offset droid brain and dedicated ordnance pod for proton torpedoes. Produced in untold millions by Baktoid Armor Workshop, Hyena Droids serve as the primary bomber element of the Confederacy’s starfighter forces. While capable of holding its own in a dogfight thanks to its high speed and respectable maneuverability, the Hyena excels in attack runs against larger targets, delivering powerful torpedo strikes before disengaging.

The Basilisk War Droid is an ancient Mandalorian assault craft, revived in modern form as a fast, heavily armored strike platform. Its forward-facing weapons suite is designed for overwhelming close-range attacks, allowing it to tear through lightly armored starfighters with devastating volleys. Foldable wings grant bursts of speed for rapid ambushes or quick disengagements, making the Basilisk a dangerous hit-and-run attacker.

True to Mandalorian Neo-Crusader doctrine, the Basilisk sacrifices shields and pilot protection in favor of brute offensive power and durability. While vulnerable to sustained fire from heavier warships, these semi-sentient war machines excel when unleashed against fighter screens, where their concentrated firepower can shred entire squadrons in moments.

Prioritizing speed and agility above all else, the elegant N-1 Starfighter is a high-performance light interceptor used exclusively by the Royal Naboo forces. Extremely small and difficult to hit, it combines rapid maneuverability with quickly recharging shields and an onboard astromech for limited in-flight repairs. These traits allow the N-1 to evade incoming fire and outmaneuver slower opponents in sustained dogfights.

However, the N-1 is lightly armed, carrying only twin repeating laser cannons and a homing torpedo launcher. While effective against lightly armored targets, it struggles to damage shielded or heavily armored craft, and can be overwhelmed by more heavily armed interceptors capable of breaching its defenses. It performs best when engaging nimble fighters where its speed and precision can be fully exploited.

Developed alongside the N-1, the N-1B Starbomber is a larger, three-seat strike variant that retains the same emphasis on speed and agility. Equipped with four engines and only slightly less maneuverable than its interceptor counterpart, the N-1B is unusually nimble for a bomber. Strong shielding, a small profile, and an onboard astromech allow it to evade incoming fire and survive attack runs that would overwhelm heavier strike craft.

The N-1B carries a payload of proton torpedoes for engaging starships and hardened targets, supported by twin light laser cannons and a rear-mounted twin laser turret for defense against pursuing fighters. While lightly armed for dogfighting and less durable than dedicated bombers, its speed and precision make it highly effective in hit-and-run strikes, slipping past defenses to deliver torpedoes before disengaging.

A byproduct of endless galactic warfare, these improvised starfighters are cobbled together from Clone Wars–era wreckage and discarded military hardware. Salvaged from junkyards and battlefield debris, they’re bolted into whatever configuration can still fly. None possess hyperdrives, relying entirely on carrier deployment. Their armor is fragile, shields are inconsistent, and only a handful have astromech repair droids. With outdated weapons and unreliable systems, their only strengths lie in their sheer numbers, low cost, and the desperation of mercenary pilots willing to die for a paycheck.

A dedicated fighter element composed of salvaged Clone Wars–era starfighters including V-19 Torrents, V-Wings, Actis- and Delta-series interceptors, Z-95CVIs, N-1 starfighters, and even manned Vulture droids. These ramshackle craft rely on overwhelming numbers and sheer volume of fire rather than precision or coordination. Against organized military squadrons, their lack of discipline, weak defenses, and inconsistent performance ensure they are quickly torn apart in combat.

20 units per squadron.

Tier I Ugly Bomber Squadron

T1_Ugly_Bomber_Squadron · Squadron
Hull20, 26, 40
Shields10, 0
Shield Regen4, 0
Cost600
Pop2
Build Time5
AI Combat Power3
Tech Level99
Speed3.0, 2.5, 3.5, 3, 4, 3.7
Squadron Size17
AffiliationNeutral, Underworld, Republic
ClassBomber, AntiFrigate
AbilitiesHUNT
Formation
10-10
Altitude

A byproduct of endless galactic warfare, these improvised starfighters are cobbled together from Clone Wars–era wreckage and discarded military hardware. Salvaged from junkyards and battlefield debris, they’re bolted into whatever configuration can still fly. None possess hyperdrives, relying entirely on carrier deployment. Their armor is fragile, shields are inconsistent, and only a handful have astromech repair droids. With outdated weapons and unreliable systems, their only strengths lie in their sheer numbers, low cost, and the desperation of mercenary pilots willing to die for a paycheck.

A dedicated bomber element built from Clone Wars–era gunships and strike craft — ARC-170s, LAATs, BTL-B Y-Wings, HMP Gunships, and even manned Hyena droid bombers. These hulking, slow vessels are designed to punch through armor and deliver heavy loads of proton torpedoes and armor-piercing missiles against hardened targets and capital ships. Their size and sluggish maneuverability make them vulnerable to enemy fighters; their mission is simple and brutal: get the payload to the target by any means available.

16 units per squadron.

Composite Squadron

Standard Ugly Starfighters equipped with a Hyperdrive allowing for use without a carrier. Several Uglies in the squadron being armed with anti-ship missles allows for basic anti-ship use while several are armed with other ordinance allowing for decent anti-starfighter attack. Shields are also featured on all of the variants in this squadron.

8 units per squadron.

Composite Squadron, Weak

A squadron of the most basic variants of Ugly Starfighters. All flying scrap metal that are armed coffins for pilots with the only benefit being low cost allowing easy replacement. Lightly armed and lower performance of the sum of their parts and lacking any heavy weapons means they can only serve as cheap escort fighters or meat shields for proper starfighters.

12 units per squadron.

SP: 60 (5/s), HP: 60, Armor: Heavy, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 2.475 Active Abilities: Lock S-Foils, Deploy Flares Passive Abilities: Beskar Armor: 35% chance to negate incoming damage 5 units per squadron.

The Mandal Hypernautics StarViper Attack Platform (SVAP-2) is the mass-producible evolution of Prince Xizor’s personal starfighter, Virago. While the Virago was meant to be the only craft of its kind, Mandal Hypernautics reacquired the production rights and designed a version suitable for mass production: the SVAP-2. Although the standard StarViper is less powerful, it remains an astonishingly advanced and capable starfighter, with the price tag to match. Extremely maneuverable thanks to its armored maneuvering fins, and highly durable due to strong shields and beskar-inlaid armor, the StarViper also features an advanced targeting system for its swiveling weapon mounts, allowing the craft to maintain an accurate and wide field of fire.

While durable, the large StarViper presents a substantial frontal target profile, making it vulnerable to even inaccurate weaponry when its S-foils are locked in the attack position. It is especially susceptible to missiles and torpedoes, relying on countermeasure flares for temporary protection. Despite this vulnerability, the StarViper is a top-of-the-line assault fighter capable of engaging a variety of targets and excelling in dogfights.

The Miy’Til Bomber is a fast, durable heavy strike craft deployed by the Hapes Consortium for precision attacks against enemy capital ships. Emphasizing speed and survivability, it can outrun most starfighters, especially when diverting additional power to its already powerful engines. Designed for rapid hit-and-run strikes, the Miy’Til can heavily debuff enemy shields and armor to support friendly fighters, or remain on target to inflict serious damage with its heavy laser cannons. Best employed against large warships, it excels at weakening hostile vessels and creating openings for the rest of the Hapan Starfleet to exploit.

This unit is unaffected by nebulas.

The GAT-12 Skipray Blastboat is a rugged gunboat-bomber hybrid developed by Republic Sienar Systems prior to the Clone Wars. Large, heavily armored, and equipped with strong shields, a missile jamming suite, and an astromech for in-flight repairs, it is designed to engage targets well above its weight class. A medium laser turret provides defensive coverage, while long-range ion cannons and a heavy payload of proton torpedoes make the Skipray especially effective against gunships and capital ships.

However, the Skipray’s size and limited speed make it an easy target for interceptors. Though highly capable, its complexity and cost prevented widespread adoption, and it was ultimately overshadowed by cheaper dedicated strike craft. Many surplus Skiprays later found service with pirates and militia forces, where their durability and firepower made them formidable bomber platforms.

The SCT-27 “Cuttlefish” Light Hauler was originally designed to ferry small cargo loads through dense asteroid fields, but has since been heavily modified by pirate groups for frontline combat. Its cargo cranes were removed and replaced with forward- and rear-facing light laser turrets, while the cargo bay was reconfigured to carry and launch a large payload of light proton torpedoes, transforming the once-innocuous hauler into a budget strike platform.

Slow, poorly maneuverable, and lightly protected, the Cuttlefish is an easy target for enemy fighters. However, if allowed to close the distance, its torpedo payload can deliver a devastating blow, making it a dangerous but expendable attacker.

SP: 250 (5/s), HP: 150 (1/s), Armor: Medium, Max Speed: 7.5, Agility: 1.5 Active Abilities: Activate SLAM Drive Passive Abilities: Astromech Repair 3 units per squadron.

Heavy Laser Cannon: 1000 m range, 24 DMG

Light High-Explosive Missile: 1000 m range, no shield penetration, 15 DMG, 35 m AOE

The massive PT-1 Gunship is a strange and unconventional design originally commissioned by the Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps of Naboo. Built as a fast anti-starfighter platform, the PT-1 is essentially two enormously powerful engines attached to a large dual crew module and a broad, one-piece armored wing that forms most of the craft’s structure. Armed with heavy laser cannons and high-explosive missiles, it was intended to obliterate enemy squadrons in a single devastating volley before retreating at extreme speed.

Outfitted with a SubLight Acceleration Motor (SLAM), the PT-1 is built for straight-line attack runs and rapid disengagements. However, it presents a large target profile, is lightly armored for a gunship, and suffers from poor maneuverability. During the Galactic Civil War, rebel cells and criminal organizations adopted the PT-1, finding its exceptional speed equally useful for hit-and-run strikes and smuggling cargo past Imperial blockades.

A mixed group of CEC YT-series light freighters, commonly used across the galaxy by traders, smugglers, and pirates due to their modular and easily modified design. While these examples lack the extensive custom upgrades seen on famous vessels like the Millennium Falcon or Outrider, they retain the durability and versatility that made the platform so popular.

Equipped with turreted laser cannons offering wide firing coverage, these freighters can function as makeshift gunships. Heavy armor and shielding allow them to absorb punishment, while their respectable agility for ships of their size lets them support starfighters and lay down sustained fire during dogfights.

A modified CEC Action-series bulk freighter, the Interceptor II is a mass-produced light corvette favored by pirates and local militias. Outfitted with six heavy laser cannons and a pair of light ion cannons, it serves as a cheap and reliable picket and screening vessel.

While its armor and shields provide moderate protection, the Interceptor II is ill-suited for direct engagements with military-grade warships unless supported in large numbers. However, its low cost and minimal crew requirements make it easy to deploy in swarms, where it can become surprisingly deadly through sheer weight of fire.

A further development of the Interceptor II, the Interceptor III is a more capable and versatile corvette suited for independent operations, scouting, and fleet support. Improved shielding, reinforced armor plating, and upgraded sublight engines provide greater survivability and agility in combat.

Its expanded armament includes dual heavy laser cannons, a dual light turbolaser turret, and light concussion missile launchers, allowing it to effectively engage enemy corvettes and threaten larger vessels. Adaptable and dependable, the Interceptor III serves as a core workhorse for underworld fleets, performing everything from patrol duties to fighter screening with ease.

A relic of the Old Republic’s golden age, the Hammerhead-class Cruiser served as a mainstay of the fleet for centuries, its iconic silhouette becoming synonymous with Republic naval power across the galaxy. Designed for long-range engagements, its forward-mounted dual turbolaser cannons could lay down precise, sustained fire on enemy vessels well before they entered retaliatory range. A small internal hangar provided space for limited fighter support or reconnaissance craft, enhancing the ship’s flexibility in battlefield roles. These features made the Hammerhead a dependable light frigate—equally suited for patrolling hyperspace lanes or forming the outer perimeter of a battle line.

However, the design’s strengths were narrowly focused. With its primary weapons fixed forward, the Hammerhead was notoriously vulnerable to flanking maneuvers and rear assaults. Aside from four medium anti-starfighter laser batteries, it lacked meaningful defensive coverage, especially against coordinated bomber strikes or more maneuverable opponents. This flaw ultimately led to its gradual retirement in favor of more versatile warships. Nevertheless, its reliability, ease of maintenance, and long service life earned it legendary status. Today, the Hammerhead lives on in reserve fleets, planetary militias, or among nostalgic admirals who favor its brutal efficiency in head-on engagements.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 3000; Hit points: 3000

Weapons: x1 Repeating Turbolaser, x1 Repeating Heavy Laser Cannon, x3 Twin Turbolaser, x4 Medium Laser Cannon

SP: 1500 (50/s), HP: 3000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 5.5, Agility: 0.425 Sensor Range: 2450m, Max Engagement Range: 3000m Active Abilities: Self-Destruct, Guidance Jammer (1500m) Passive Abilities: Light Tractor Beam

Weapons: x2 Medium Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher, x4 Dual Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x12 Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Light Concussion Missile Launcher

Marketed by Corellian Engineering Corporation as a low-cost export model, the U-571-class Heavy Gunship was offered to planetary defense forces, independent governments, and private buyers across the galaxy. To reduce production costs and satisfy export restrictions, the vessel omitted many of the advanced fire-control systems and specialized munitions found aboard the Rebel variant. Even so, its combination of heavy flak laser cannons, medium laser cannons, and numerous light concussion missile launchers still made it an effective escort vessel against starfighters, bombers, and other light craft.

The Galactic Empire largely dismissed the design in favor of domestically produced escort ships, while criminal organizations valued it primarily for its low cost and ease of maintenance. As a final safeguard against capture, every export-model U-571 was equipped with a built-in self-destruct system, allowing desperate crews to cripple nearby enemy vessels rather than surrender their ship intact.

Fighter 7·Bomber 7·Gunship 7·Transport 7·Corvette 7·Frigate 7·Capital 7·SpaceStructure 7·Super 7

Originally a civilian freighter, the Longhorn-class Frigate was repurposed by criminal syndicates and warlords into a frontline combat vessel. Its former cargo bays were stripped out and replaced with medium mass driver emplacements, giving it formidable broadside capabilities for its size. Though its armor plating is relatively modest, it houses two heavy laser turrets for basic self-defense—barely adequate against determined bomber strikes. Its true strength lies in its role as a long-range support ship, using its slow-firing but armor-piercing mass drivers to supplement larger fleet engagements. While its firing arc is limited, and it offers little protection against starfighters, in the right formation it can bring down enemy capital ships piece by piece—one thunderous impact at a time.

SP: 2500 (30/s) HP: 3250, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 4.5, Agility: 0.65 Sensor Range: 1850m, Max Engagement Range: 3000m Active Abilities: Power To Weapons Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x4 ASC Missile Launcher, x4 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x4 Dual Light Turbolaser

Developed by Kuat Drive Yards shortly before the Clone Wars, the Arquitens-class was quickly integrated into the Republic Navy and saw widespread deployment across nearly every major theater. Originally intended for patrol, picket, and escort duties, the Arquitens proved highly adaptable in frontline engagements. Armed with light turbolasers, heavy laser cannons, and anti-strikecraft concussion (ASC) missiles, it is well equipped for both ship-to-ship combat and fighter screening.

What sets it apart from other corvettes of the era is its impressive speed and agility, allowing it to chase down fleeing targets and reposition quickly in battle. With a balanced mix of firepower, mobility, and moderate durability, the Arquitens serves as a flexible all-rounder capable of fulfilling many roles, though exceptional in none.

Known in Mando’a as “Ambush,” the Je’Havey is a compact but heavily armored assault ship developed by the Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders for shock warfare. Armed with rapid-firing turbolasers, ion cannons, and concussion missile launchers, it was designed to operate in coordinated packs, encircling enemy formations and annihilating them under a relentless crossfire. Though officially classified as a corvette due to its size, the Je’Havey carries the armor protection and offensive output of a light frigate, making it far deadlier than its silhouette suggests and a terror in close-range fleet actions.

The Carrack-class light frigate is a compact, well-armed warship capable of engaging a wide range of targets. Equipped with anti-shield, anti-ship, and anti-starfighter weaponry, it poses a serious threat to corvettes, frigates, and strikecraft alike. However, its relatively weak reactor and shield generator limit its durability in prolonged engagements.

Designed for efficiency and ease of production, the Carrack serves well as an escort vessel and excels when deployed in wolfpack formations, where its versatile loadout and ion weaponry can overwhelm larger targets.

Klay Maro, president of the Sons of the Void – Outer Rim Chapter, commands a loose brotherhood of outlaw spacers operating beyond Imperial authority. Engaged in weapons trafficking, spice running, contract killings, and piracy, the gang thrives in the lawless reaches of the Outer Rim. From the bridge of his customized EF76 Nebulon-B frigate, Reaper’s Gavel, Klay leads his lieutenants—each commanding their own modified Corellian CR90 corvette—in a roaming campaign of profit and destruction, leaving a trail of chaos in their wake.

Hapan Battle Dragon: The primary ship of the line for the Hapan Royal Navy, the Battle Dragon is as elegant as it is efficient. It maintains a surprising volume of firepower on a single target by synchronizing its weapon reload cycle with the rotation of its dual dish-mounted turrets. Despite its relatively small size, this allows the Dragon to unleash a concentrated hail of turbolaser and ion cannon fire. However, this optimized firing pattern can only be directed at one target at a time, limiting its effectiveness against multiple enemies.

Max speed: 3.0; Shieldpoints: 8000; Hitpoints: 8000

Originally designed by SoroSuub as a long-range cargo hauler, the Quasar Fire-class Bulk Cruiser was never intended for frontline combat. With the outbreak of the Galactic Civil War, however, these freighters were hastily converted for military service by the Rebel Alliance and other sympathetic factions desperate for transport capacity. Robust, reliable, inexpensive, and easy to modify, the Quasar is commonly repurposed as a mobile hangar and supply ship, capable of ferrying large numbers of starfighters, troops, and vital materiel across the galaxy. Respectable armor and a modest weapons suite provide basic protection, but weak shields and painfully slow speed leave the Quasar best employed well behind the front lines.

The Quasar Fire-class Carrier grants all friendly fighters, bombers, and gunships +5% hull strength, +5% shield strength, and +10% movement speed.

The Bothan Assault Frigate 4 (BAF-4), produced by Bothawui Shipyards, was envisioned as a versatile backbone warship that could be deployed in large numbers across the front. Outfitted with strong shields but relatively weak armor, the BAF-4 relied on staying power rather than brute endurance. Its varied and extensive armament—including ion cannons, heavy laser cannons, advanced proton torpedoes, concussion missile launchers, dual turbolasers, and heavy flak lasers—allowed it to effectively engage a wide array of targets.

A spacious internal hangar housed up to four squadrons of mixed strike craft, giving the frigate added flexibility in fleet actions. Though it lacked specialization in any one area, its balanced design made the BAF-4 a dependable jack-of-all-trades vessel, capable of adapting to whatever the battlefield demanded—so long as it wasn’t outmatched in raw firepower or durability.

Max speed: 4.35; Shield points: 12000; Hit points: 9500

SP: 10000 (100/s); HP: 11500, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.75, Agility: 0.2 Active Abilities: Power To Weapons, Medium Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x8 Triple Turbolaser, x22 Heavy Laser Cannon

Complement: 1 Tier II Ugly Fighter Squadron (1), 1 Tier II Ugly Bomber Squadron (1)

Designed and produced by Rendilli StarDrive decades before the Clone Wars, the Neutron Star–class was an early Republic-era frigate intended to serve dual roles as both a warship and a bulk transport. Often referred to simply as a “bulk cruiser,” the class became a common sight along major trade routes and patrol sectors, its silhouette familiar enough to be casually dismissed by smugglers and spacers alike. By the time of the Clone Wars, however, the design was already showing its age, having been eclipsed by newer and more capable Rendilli warships such as the Dreadnaught-class Heavy Cruiser. As a result, the Neutron Star saw only limited frontline service and was largely relegated to secondary duties.

During the Galactic Civil War, the Neutron Star endured as a cheap and readily available alternative to modern capital ships, pressed into service by the Empire and local defense forces for patrol and anti-piracy operations. Armed with several triple turbolasers and numerous heavy laser cannons, it is capable of delivering steady, sustained fire, but its complete lack of ion weaponry or missile launchers leaves it poorly suited to engaging heavily shielded or armored opponents. Mediocre armor protection, merely adequate shields, and a small starfighter complement further underscore its limitations. Long obsolete as a true warship, the Neutron Star nonetheless lives on in widespread use among criminal syndicates and paramilitary forces, valued not for its strength, but for its availability, simplicity, and low cost.

Developed by Sienar Fleet Systems, the Vindicator-class was designed to fill a role often neglected by the Tarkin Doctrine: a medium-sized, general-purpose heavy frigate. Armed with accurate long-range heavy turbolasers supported by standard and light turbolasers, ion cannons, and heavy laser cannons, the Vindicator can engage and defeat a wide range of targets with ease. Its effectiveness in combat quickly led to widespread production across Imperial shipyards, making it a common sight in major theaters of the Galactic Civil War.

SP: 10000 (100/s) HP: 12500, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 4, Agility: 0.465 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 3250m Active Abilities: Deploy Fighter Repair Droids Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x4 Ion Cannon, x4 Quad Turbolaser, x8 Concussion Missile Launcher

Complement: 2 I-Wing Squadron (8), 2 Z-95 Hullcracker Squadron (8)

Designed as a fast attack carrier, the Dor’bulla Strike Carrier serves as the backbone of Hutt starfighter operations and one of the few dedicated support vessels in the fleet. Featuring the largest hangar complement of any Hutt warship, the Dor’bulla provides essential fighter cover to compensate for the poor anti-starfighter defenses common among heavier Hutt vessels. Though lightly armed on its own, it performs best alongside ships such as the Darran-Tan Destroyer and Chelandion Heavy Cruiser, supporting their heavy firepower with starfighters and ion cannons capable of weakening enemy shields.

Unlike the heavily armored bruisers that dominate Hutt fleets, the Dor’bulla relies on speed, maneuverability, and powerful engines to survive. Quad turbolasers provide limited protection against lighter warships, while concussion missile launchers offer a useful deterrent against bombers. However, weak shielding and lackluster armor leave the Dor’bulla highly vulnerable if caught in direct combat without support.

This starship costs 100 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

SP: 20000 (400/s) HP: 12500, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 4, Agility: 0.465 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 3250m Active Abilities: Deploy Fighter Repair Droids, Solar Weapon Surge Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

A product of Jabba Desilijic Tiure’s ambitious Kajidic Project, this enhanced variant of the Dor’bulla-class improves upon the original design in nearly every regard. Alongside upgraded shield generators for improved survivability, the Kajidic Dor’bulla carries twice the number of quad turbolasers found on the standard model, replaces its ion cannons with dual mounts, and adds two dual medium turbolasers, dramatically increasing its effectiveness against enemy warships.

Its expanded hangar complement is further strengthened by more advanced starfighters, transforming the Kajidic Dor’bulla into a significantly more capable carrier and fleet support vessel. Retaining the speed and maneuverability of the original while addressing many of its combat shortcomings, the Kajidic variant serves as one of the most versatile ships in the Hutt fleet.

This starship costs 200 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Javelin-class Heavy Thrustship Built for the ruthless, the Javelin-class heavy thrustship is Black Sun’s answer to a fast, armored battering ram in space. Designed as a personal command vessel for syndicate lieutenants, it trades elegance for brute force—wrapped in durasteel and driven by oversized engines that don’t care how they get in or out. Most of its mass is armor and propulsion, not weapons. It packs four quad turbolasers, ion cannons, and high-explosive missile launchers—enough to carve through mid-size threats, but not meant to duel capital ships head-on.

What the Javelin lacks in firepower, it makes up for in grit. A quick-jolt power-to-shields system gives it a second wind in battle, and its rugged frame can absorb punishment that would cripple most ships its size. It’s not refined. It’s not subtle. But when you fly Black Sun colors, survival is the only luxury that matters.

Max speed: 5.25; Shield points: 5000; Hit points: 20000

Weapons: x1 Heavy Laser Cannon, x2 HE Missile Launcher, x4 Ion Cannon, x4 Quad Turbolaser

SP: 15000 (125/s) HP: 30000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.065 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 4500m Active Abilities: Heavy Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x1 Heavy Mass Driver, x1 Heavy Turbolaser, x2 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x4 Quad Turbolaser, x20 Heavy Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher

The Invincible-class Heavy Cruiser is an aging warship dating back to the Old Republic, designed during an era when massive capital ships ruled the stars before advances in weapons and starfighter technology rendered many such vessels obsolete. Surprisingly cheap and easy to acquire in the modern age, these cruisers are best suited for anti-piracy operations and fleet fire support rather than frontline engagements.

Its primary armament, consisting of a heavy mass driver and a heavy turbolaser, are fixed forward, while multiple quad turbolasers and heavy laser cannons provide flank coverage. Secondary weapons include a complement of heavy armor-piercing missiles capable of devastating armored targets with ease. However, lacking ion weaponry, the Invincible-class struggles against heavily shielded opponents and is utterly defenseless against bomber attacks.

This starship costs 200 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Required Planets (Empire, Neutral, CIS, Rebel, Republic, Underworld): Etti_IV, Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

A modified Providence Destroyer of one of the last the Separatist Holdouts. When all others joined the Rebel Alliance, Captain Khemry remained loyal to the ideals of the CIS and his personal hero General Grievous. With secret backing from the Banking Clans, Khemry has harassed Imperial operations around the systems of Muunilinst and Mygeeto and policed the sector of Rebel activity for being Republic dogs. Quickly these practices turned into outright piracy and raids turned to civilian vessels and the Banking Clans were paying for protection or ransoms. Khemry and his holdout faction became known as the wealthiest pirate gangs in the galaxy known as the Bone Giants for the many large Kaleesh warriors and their face bones.

Providence "Dreadnought" variant with improved Calamari shields and Heavy Concussion Missile Launchers instead of Proton Torpedo Launchers.

A Dauntless-class Cruiser that led a group of Sullustians in their revolt again the Empire. A Kandosii Battleship under the command of a former Death Watch who claims to be the descendant of some great gladiator from the crusades. Kas along with a group of his allies held out when they the Death Watch defeated by Mandalore Spar and his Mandalorian Protectors. He took the last of the Death Watch, an ancient warship in disrepair even though the Beskar hull remained untouched by time, and waged a personal war against Spar's CIS supporters and the Republic invaders before being forced to piracy to survive the Imperial Age and fled Mandalore. When Mandal Hypernautics were under constant raids from the Zann Consortium they pair a handsome bounty and upgraded their vessel with new Mandalorian tech. The infamous Alor'ad and his gang had gathered many likeminded Mando'ade and soon fought off the Consortium piracy efforts only to take their place and use the Mandalore System and their gathered fleet to rule piracy in the sector.

Kandosii Battleship with premium Beskar Armor, Heavy Mass Drivers replacing the missile launchers, and a Point Defense Laser system.

Once the backbone of the Mandalorian Neo-Crusader fleet during the Mandalorian Wars, the Kyramud-class Battleship is a relic of brutalist warship design. Despite its imposing insectoid frame and sheer mass, the Kyramud carries surprisingly limited direct-fire weaponry for a ship of its size. Instead, it leans into overwhelming resilience—encased in a near-impenetrable beskar shell and protected by a shield generator of absurd output, the Kyramud is notoriously difficult to bring down. Its primary offensive capability lies in long-range bombardment, unleashing devastating volleys from ten heavy concussion missile launchers. Supported by a contingent of Basilisk war droids for close defense and boarding actions, the Kyramud is less a brawler and more a slow-moving fortress—unyielding, unrelenting, and built to endure.

Max speed: 2.0; Shield points: 100000; Hit points: 35000

Weapons: x1 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x2 Quad Medium Turbolaser, x2 Heavy Ion Cannon, Heavy Concussion Missile System (10 missiles)

Complement: 2 Basilisk Wardroid Squadron (6)

This starship costs 500 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Named after the capital city of Mandalore, the Keldabe-class embodies the raw strength and unrelenting aggression of Mandalorian war doctrine. Its weapon systems include dual heavy ion cannons and dual heavy turbolasers for long-range engagements, supported by standard dual turbolasers and heavy laser cannons for brutal close-range brawling. The ship’s most fearsome weapons, however, are its heavy and ultra-heavy mass drivers, mounted in armored beskar housings and capable of tearing through enemy warships before they ever get into range. Designed to go head-to-head with the strongest ships in the galaxy, the Keldabe is widely regarded as one of the most feared capital ships in known space.

Max Speed: 3; Shieldpoints: 25000; Hitpoints: 50000

Weapons: x2 Super Heavy Mass Driver, x4 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x6 Heavy Mass Driver, x12 Dual Turbolaser, x12 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x20 Heavy Laser Cannon

This starship costs 1180 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Built in a bygone age of conquest by the Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders, the Kandosii-class Star Dreadnought embodies the brutal, no-nonsense doctrine of Mandalorian warfare. Designed with zero regard for elegance or subtlety, the Kandosii overwhelmed enemies with sheer firepower—and it still does. Armed with ultra-heavy assault concussion missile launchers and heavy turbolasers, reinforced by layered plating and powerful shield generators, and supported by integrated hangars, this dreadnought is a relic in name only. Though born of an older era, it remains fully capable of slugging it out with modern warships.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 40000; Hit points: 64000

Weapons: x2 Super Heavy Turbolaser, x3 Quad Medium Turbolaser, x6 Dual Turbolaser, Ultra Heavy Concussion Missile System (8 missiles)

Complement: 2 Basilisk Wardroid Squadron (2)

This starship costs 720 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Required Planets (Empire, CIS, Rebel, Republic, Underworld): Mandalore, MalachorV, Lehon

SP: 55000 (500/s) HP: 75000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.5, Agility: 0.075 Active Abilities: Sensor Ping, Sensor Jamming Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x8 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x26 Quad Turbolaser

Complement: 14 Vulture Droid Squadron (154)

Designed and built by Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc. as the LH-3210 Cargo Freighter, the Lucrehulk-class was purchased in large numbers by the Trade Federation and later, the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Originally armed to deter rampant piracy along major trade routes, the Lucrehulk’s immense size and structural strength made it well suited for further militarization. With relatively minor modifications, these armed freighters were converted into full warships and redesignated as Lucrehulk-class Carriers or Droid Control Ships. In this role, they carried thousands of droid starfighters, millions of battle droids, and hundreds of combat vehicles, allowing a single vessel to blockade, assault, and occupy entire planets with minimal support.

This starship costs 1800 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

SP: 75000 (750/s) HP: 125000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.075 Active Abilities: Full Salvo (Turbolasers) Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x16 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x38 Quad Turbolaser

Complement: 10 Vulture Droid Squadron (90)

Many Lucrehulk-class carriers were modified into dedicated battlecruisers. Featuring reinforced armor plating, additional quad turbolaser batteries linked to advanced targeting systems, and more powerful shield generators, these warships could outgun most Republic vessels and can still stand up to many heavy Star Destroyers today.

Despite their increased protection and firepower, they are ironically more vulnerable to bomber attacks than their carrier counterparts. Their quad heavy laser cannons are designed to supplement the main turbolaser batteries and lack the accuracy needed to reliably engage enemy starfighters.

Required Planets (Neutral, Rebel, Underworld): Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost, MonCalamari
Special Structures (CSA): Minor_Shipyard_CSA

Special Structures (Underworld): U_Shipyard_3

The Harrower-class was the spearhead of the resurgent Sith Empire, a symbol of terror and dominance during the Great Galactic War. Towering and heavily armored, it bristles with turbolasers across its angular hull, delivering devastating broadsides that could shatter even the most stalwart Republic defenses. Its cavernous hangars unleash wings of Sith starfighters, ensuring supremacy in both fleet battles and planetary sieges. Though slower and less maneuverable than some of its rivals, the Harrower compensates with sheer firepower, resilience, and intimidation. With reinforced shielding and layered armor, it endures punishment that would cripple lesser warships, while its presence alone strikes fear into enemy fleets. More than just a warship, the Harrower is a dreadnought in the truest sense — an enduring testament to the might and ambition of the Sith.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 150000 (500/s); Hit points: 235000

Weapons: x6 Ion Cannon, x16 Turbolaser, x21 Octuple Turbolaser

Complement: 12 Sith Starfighter Squadron (36), 6 Sith Aurora Bomber Squadron (18)

This starship costs 3400 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

The Lusankya was captured by the New Republic, a sister ship to the Executor. The New Republic refitted her with better armor than Star Dreadnoughts still in Imperial service, several other systems were also redesigned.

During the Yuuzhan Vong War she participated in the Battle of Borleias, where she helped protect the Republic stronghold on Borleias over the course of a month. After taking heavy damage due to attrition, it was decided that she would be abandoned. When the time came to finally evacuate Borleias, the Lusankya was sent to collide into the Domain Hul worldship.

While capable of long range bombardment, she is most effective at close range and engaging multiple targets at once. Vulnerable to bombers.

Max speed: 6; Shield points: 400000; Hit points: 600000; 6 A-Wing (94), 6 Y-Wing (54), 2 A/SF-01-Elite (18)

This starship costs 18500 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Required Planets: Byss, Kuat, Fondor, MonCalamari
Special Structures: R_Shipyard_3
